+title: 'Model: ConnectionModel request-scoped elicitations, removed when their request finishes'
+---
+## What
+Add request-scoped elicitations to `ConnectionModel` in `Sources/FoundationModelsACPClient/Model/ConnectionModel+Elicitation.swift`.
+
+Upstream API (foundationmodelsacp-c7, task ^swjqyk4): `ClientSideConnection` gives outgoing request events `.started(id, method)` and `.finished(id)` (success, error, cancel, close), and a method lookup for an in-flight id. The elicitation `scope` is `.session(ElicitationSessionScope)` or `.request(ElicitationRequestScope)`, and `ElicitationRequestScope.requestId: RequestId` names the client request. The schema does not limit which methods can cause one (auth/login is the usual one). Use the final names from gate task 81s5j74.
+
+- [ ] `pendingElicitations: [PendingElicitation]` on ConnectionModel, each item with its `requestId` and the method name of that request (from the lookup), so the UI can show which operation asked. Reply methods: `acceptElicitation(_:content:)`, `declineElicitation(_:)`, `cancelElicitation(_:)`. Reuse `PendingRequestStates`.
+- [ ] `ModelClient.createElicitation` sends `.request` scope items here (task jge1qvf routes `.session` scope).
+- [ ] At connect, start one task that reads the request events. On `.finished(id)`, cancel and remove every pending elicitation with that `requestId`.
+- [ ] On disconnect or failure, cancel every request-scope item.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] A request-scope elicitation that the agent sends during `auth/login` shows in `pendingElicitations` with `requestId` and method `auth/login`.
+- [ ] When that request completes or fails, the item is removed and the agent receives `cancel` (if it was not answered).
+- [ ] Accept, decline and cancel resume the agent's call exactly one time.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] New `Tests/FoundationModelsACPClientTests/Model/ConnectionModelElicitationTests.swift` over `InMemoryTransport.pair()` with a scripted agent that sends a request-scope elicitation while it handles `auth/login`: the three replies, removal on request success, removal on request error, removal on disconnect.
+- [ ] `swift test --filter ConnectionModelElicitationTests` passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file

+    - Existing `ModelClientTests.aRequestScopedElicitationGoesToTheConnectionHookThatAnswersCancel` sends a request id that is not in flight, so it still gets `cancel`.

+    - `ConnectionModel` holds a `PendingRequestQueue<PendingElicitation, CreateElicitationResponse>` and one `requestWatch` task per connection. `connect` starts the task from `subscribeToOutgoingRequests()`; `.finished(id)` cancels each item with that `requestId`. `connectionDidClose` (disconnected and failed) and each new `connect` cancel the task and every item.
